messages.content: How much electricity will I need for my 2000 sq ft home?

function.name: solar_panel_calculate_need
function.description: Calculate the number of solar panels needed for a house based on the square footage and average sunlight hours. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

square_footage.description: The square footage of the house. This is a float type value.

average_sunlight_hours.description: The average hours of sunlight received. This is a float type value.

usage_efficiency.description: The efficiency of energy usage in the home, default is 0.8. This is a float type value.

But they didn't provide average sunlight hours or usage efficiency. We could ask them for those values. Or we can assume defaults: average sunlight hours maybe 5 hours per day? usage_efficiency default 0.8. For US average ~1 kWh per square foot per year? Actually typical residential consumption ~10 kWh per square foot per year? Wait typical US household uses about 10,000 kWh per year for 2,000 sq ft -> 5 kWh per sq ft per year. So daily ~27 kWh. But we can also compute using the function: It calculates number of solar panels needed given square footage and average sunlight hours. That returns number of panels.
